name: Differentiable Moment Bounds
definition: A technique that utilizes the property that moment-based bounds $L(x)$ and $U(x)$ are continuously differentiable with respect to the moment parameters $m_i$. This enables their use in differentiable rendering pipelines where gradients with respect to scene parameters (which affect moments) are required.
summary: Differentiable Moment Bounds computes continuously differentiable upper and lower bounds on cumulative mass using arbitrary moment sequences, offering tighter, numerically stable results than standard Chebyshev-based methods for differentiable rendering.
